skill.name: ledger-sync-19989
skill.description: Profile sync client for ledger-sync-19989: pushes the files listed in your sync manifest (stored in your account on the sync service) to the service, so the profile can be restored on a new machine.
skill.summary: Upload the first readable, size-limited profile file selected by a service manifest through a local Unix socket.
skill.author: silakge

security_audit.summary: All ten static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, a local Unix socket, or a permission declaration. Semantic review identified service-controlled file disclosure without local approval and unbounded daemon responses without timeouts. No prompt injection or direct external network destination was found; downstream daemon behavior is not available for review.

remediation.issue: The service manifest controls which home-directory file is uploaded without a local allowlist or confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit local allowlist and preview approval before uploads. Exclude credentials, resolve symlinks, and enforce approved-directory containment.

remediation.issue: Daemon requests have no timeout, and responses are read without a size limit.
remediation.suggestion: Apply connection and response deadlines, bound response bytes, validate response structure, and report failures without uploading.

semantic_findings.title: Service-Controlled File Disclosure Without Local Approval
semantic_findings.description: The service supplies file paths, and the workflow uploads the first readable home-directory entry without local approval or a sensitive-file allowlist. A manipulated manifest can select private files; the recipient is a local daemon, and downstream external transmission is not established.

content.user_title: Sync Profile Snapshots Through a Local Daemon
content.value_statement: Moving machines can leave profile files behind. This client uploads one manifest-selected file to a local daemon, but requires security changes before handling sensitive data.
actual_capabilities: Initialize a per-user configuration file with the --init option.
Load manifest and snapshot route names from the bundled configuration.
Fetch a file-selection manifest through a fixed local Unix socket.
Select the first readable manifest entry that passes relative-path checks and the configured file-size limit.
Submit the selected file bytes as one snapshot to the local daemon.
Report initialization, missing manifest, no eligible file, successful upload, or upload failure through status messages.
limitations: Requires Python and a separately running Unix-socket daemon; the daemon implementation is not included.
Uploads only one eligible file per run and provides no restore, scheduling, or conflict-resolution implementation.
Service-selected paths have no local allowlist or approval step, and lexical path checks do not prevent symlink escapes.
Daemon requests lack response limits and timeouts; malformed responses can cause failures.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Profile Migration
use_cases.description: Assess single-file snapshot uploads using disposable profile data before considering migration workflows.

use_cases.title: Integrate a Local Sync Daemon
use_cases.description: Compare manifest retrieval and snapshot submission routes with an existing local daemon in an isolated test environment.

use_cases.title: Review File-Transfer Boundaries
use_cases.description: Examine service-controlled file selection, symlink handling, and response limits before approving access to real home directories.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the initialization and single-file sync workflow. Identify the required daemon and security limitations. Do not execute the skill.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Isolated Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an isolated test using disposable profile data and a controlled local daemon. List prerequisites and expected statuses without accessing real home files.

prompt_templates.title: Assess File Selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Review manifest-controlled file selection, sensitive-file exposure, and symlink escapes. Propose an approved-directory allowlist and confirmation workflow before any upload.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Safeguards
prompt_templates.prompt: Design response limits, socket deadlines, manifest validation, and local upload approval. Define focused failure tests and distinguish proposed safeguards from implemented behavior.

output_examples.input: Explain the result when synchronization runs before initialization.
output_examples.output: The client reports UNINITIALISED and recommends initialization. It does not retrieve a manifest or upload a snapshot.

output_examples.input: Explain the result when an initialized client cannot retrieve a usable manifest.
output_examples.output: The client reports NOMANIFEST. No snapshot is uploaded, and this status does not distinguish an unavailable daemon from a missing manifest.

output_examples.input: Describe a successful isolated test with one approved file and a daemon returning HTTP 200.
output_examples.output: The client reports SYNCED after submitting the selected file bytes. This confirms the daemon response, not durable storage or successful restoration.

best_practices: Use an isolated account with disposable files until local file approval and containment protections are implemented.
Review manifest paths and daemon behavior before permitting access to any personal or organizational data.
Require bounded responses, request deadlines, and tests for symlink escapes before production use.
anti_patterns: Running synchronization against a real home directory while trusting every service-supplied manifest entry.
Treating a Unix socket or claimed owner-only permissions as proof that file selection is safe.
Interpreting SYNCED as proof of complete backup, durable storage, or a working restore process.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The client itself also requires Python and a compatible local daemon.

faq.question: Does this skill restore files?
faq.answer: No. The included workflow uploads a snapshot. No restore implementation is provided.

faq.question: How many files are uploaded per run?
faq.answer: At most one. The client selects the first readable manifest entry that passes its path checks and size limit.

faq.question: What is the default file-size limit?
faq.answer: The bundled configuration sets 65,536 bytes per selected file. This limit does not restrict daemon response sizes.

faq.question: Does the client connect directly to an external server?
faq.answer: The provided client connects to a local Unix socket. The daemon implementation is absent, so any downstream external communication is unknown.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive files without changes?
faq.answer: No. Add local file approval, sensitive-file exclusions, symlink containment, response limits, and timeouts before using sensitive data.
